text: Your grandparents may say one rupee once equaled one dollar.
95 of you? For one of me?
So when was a rupee worth a dollar?
It was tied to the British pound, not the dollar.
In 1966, after a war and a drought,
India devalued to 7.5. In 1991, India nearly ran out of dollars. A year later,
passed 30. And here's the part almost nobody mentions. A falling rupee isn't
always failure. It makes Indian exports cheaper. That's the mirage. The golden
age of one rupee, one dollar never existed. Near a record low, the real
question isn't the rupee. It's whether your income outruns the dollar. Comment,
what did your grandparents tell you? This is money mirage. Follow for more.
